reuse.why: Folds the five copied provider link functions into one linkExternalAccount and the Pluggy/Akahu download copies into one downloader, reusing findOrCreateBank, syncAccount and handleSyncResponse; the takeover step re-writes unlinkAccount's local field reset instead of sharing it.

duplication.why: Removes large existing duplication across providers; the one new copy is the block of nulled sync fields used to unlink the previous holder, identical to the update inside unlinkAccount.

placement.why: Link rules (duplicate-link check, closed-account refusal, takeover) sit in the single server-side link path in accounts/app.ts, and the Fintegra download sits with the other providers in sync.ts and server-config.

scope.why: Every edit serves the four steps; the provider consolidation is broad but is what makes the rules apply once, and the desktop-client edits are needed for the exhaustive provider records.

maintainability.why: A single link pipeline with explicit per-provider variations (bankKey, fileId, syncedTables, mask) is easy to own; the inline unlink copy and the growing provider if-chains in sync.ts are the remaining weak points.

bypasses_abstraction.where: linkExternalAccount unlinks the previous holder with its own db.updateAccount of the nulled sync fields rather than a shared local-unlink step extracted from unlinkAccount (which it cannot call as is because that also contacts GoCardless).

disguised_duplication.where: The unlink field reset is an open copy of unlinkAccount's update, not reshaped; the provider wrappers are thin parameterisations, not copies.

abstraction_drift.where: linkExternalAccount gains replaceExistingLink for step 4 (a requested option, not a special case); its fileId/syncedTables/mask parameters carry pre-existing per-provider differences explicitly; all provider link handlers, including Fintegra, route through it. The fintegra branch added to processBankSyncDownload's akahu condition follows that file's existing per-provider dispatch.
